candidates.name: Flowpay
candidates.description: Prague-based embedded lending infrastructure using data and AI to give SMEs working-capital financing inside partner platforms; launched in the Netherlands in 2025.

evidence.claim: Secured €30M from Fasanara Capital for SME working-capital financing and embedded finance (March 2025).
Launched in the Netherlands with a €30M facility from Fasanara Capital.
Total funding $35.8M, latest round March 2025, expanding embedded lending infrastructure.

traction.rationale: Expanding from CZ/SK to Netherlands; no volume/revenue figures sourced.

funding.rationale: €30M debt facility from Fasanara (2025); ~$35.8M total per press; mostly debt, not equity.

differentiation.rationale: Embedded lending infrastructure with AI risk assessment; data-driven underwriting is hard to copy.

regulatory.rationale: Licensing/partner-lender setup not verified in my sources.

candidates.name: Montonio
candidates.description: Tallinn-based all-in-one checkout platform for e-commerce SMBs: bank-link payments, cards, BLIK in Poland, shipping logistics and embedded BNPL/financing.

evidence.claim: Raised €11M Series A led by Index Ventures.
Expanded from open banking payments into card payments, BLIK, shipping logistics and embedded BNPL/financing.
Exclusive financing partnership with licensed bank Inbank.

traction.rationale: Multi-country Baltic coverage, Poland expansion, bank partnership; no volume numbers.

funding.rationale: €11M Series A led by Index Ventures; dated (2022).

differentiation.rationale: Bundle of payments, BNPL and logistics for SMB merchants; competitors are numerous.

theme_fit.rationale: Embedded payments and checkout financing; CEE/Baltics.

regulatory.rationale: Financing delivered through licensed bank Inbank.

candidates.name: Wallester
candidates.description: Estonian licensed payment institution and Visa Principal Member offering white-label card issuing, accounts and payment infrastructure to businesses across the EEA and UK.

evidence.claim: Estonian FSA-regulated payment institution and Visa Principal Member; card issuing across EEA and UK.
Named #1 fastest-growing company in its category in FT1000 2026.
Founded 2016; scaled into a licensed Visa Principal Member.

traction.rationale: FT1000 2026 #1 fastest-growing in fintech/financial services category; serves EEA and UK.

differentiation.rationale: Direct Visa Principal Membership and PCI DSS Level 1 white-label issuing.

candidates.name: Paynetics
candidates.description: Sofia-based e-money institution offering acquiring, card issuing, e-wallets, account management and banking-as-a-service to fintechs and brands.

evidence.claim: Closed a €2.5M round (2020) from New Vision 3 and Bulgarian American Credit Bank; full-stack acquiring, issuing, e-wallet and account management.
Named among regulated European embedded finance infrastructure providers.

traction.rationale: Recognised as a European regulated BaaS provider; no volume data.

regulatory.rationale: E-money institution per sources; licence details not directly verified.

candidates.name: Wealthon
candidates.description: Warsaw-based SME finance ecosystem: POS-terminal-turnover financing (Poscash), a business finance management app (Wallet) and payment tools; sells receivables to bank partners including UniCredit under a BaaS-style agreement.

evidence.claim: Raised €115.5M (PLN 531M) in Feb 2025; debt financing from Fortress Investment Group and equity from 3TS plus angels.
Equity from 3TS and angel investors in the round.
UniCredit signed a three-year agreement for up to PLN 0.5bn (EUR 115M) of SME receivables; Wealthon revenue just under PLN 30M (EUR 6.9M) in 2025.
Fortress Investment Group debt financing round recorded.

traction.rationale: ~PLN 30M revenue in 2025 and a UniCredit receivables-purchase deal of up to PLN 0.5bn.

funding.rationale: €115.5M in Feb 2025 incl. Fortress debt and 3TS equity; largest in set, though mostly debt.

differentiation.rationale: Ecosystem of POS-based financing, wallet app; own-ecosystem approach, but more lender than infrastructure.

theme_fit.rationale: Embedded SME lending via payment terminals and bank BaaS partnership; Poland.

regulatory.rationale: Funding backed by regulated bank partner UniCredit; own licences not verified.

candidates.name: PayPo
candidates.description: Warsaw-based BNPL provider embedded in e-commerce checkouts, described as Poland's largest BNPL solution, monetising both merchants and shoppers.

evidence.claim: Established 2017; described as the largest BNPL provider in Poland, monetising merchants and consumers.
Employee range 101-250 and ranked top Polish payments startup.
Directory lists total funding between €10M and €25M (sources conflict; not precisely verified).

traction.rationale: Described as Poland's largest BNPL provider, 101-250 staff.

funding.rationale: Funding figures conflict across databases; unverified.

differentiation.rationale: Market leadership in one country; BNPL is commoditising.

regulatory.rationale: Licensing not verified in my sources.

market_facts.claim: Startups in Central and Eastern Europe raised €1.83 billion from January to September 2026, up 25% from €1.46 billion a year earlier; Baltic startups raised €326 million of it versus €506 million in the same months of 2025.
From January to September 2026, Czech startups raised the most capital in CEE (€513 million) and Polish startups closed the most rounds (67).
Regulated infrastructure providers such as Solaris, Paynetics, Modulr, Swan, Treezor, Vodeno and OpenPayd supply ledgers, payment rails and card issuing to European embedded finance.

Inbank is a fintech with an EU banking licence connecting merchants, consumers and financial institutions on an embedded finance platform; it partners with 5,400+ merchants and has 865,000+ active contracts (per Fintech Baltic listing).
Inbank entered an exclusive partnership with Montonio to offer flexible financing at checkout.
Wallester was named the #1 fastest-growing company in the Fintech, Financial Services & Insurance category in the Financial Times FT1000 2026.
Embedded finance is the broader category including BaaS plus card issuing, payments, lending, AP/AR, payroll and compliance; BaaS is the subset focused on regulated banking products from a bank.

Inbank and Eurobank agreed to establish a 50/50 embedded finance joint venture in Greece; Inbank has 6,200+ merchant partners, 847,000+ active contracts, 7 European markets, and its bonds are listed on Nasdaq Tallinn.
UniCredit is scaling its Banking-as-a-Service strategy in Europe via a three-year, up to PLN 0.5bn (EUR 115M) SME receivables agreement with Polish Wealthon.
A PragmaGO report claims embedded lending boosts SME growth by up to 36% in Poland (vendor-sourced claim).
Tracxn tracks 49 embedded lending companies in Eastern Europe, 22 of them funded.
